tasks.spec:
You are revising a text-message appointment-recall pathway generator you previously built. A senior reviewer returned REVISE with nine findings, one of them blocking a patient-safety defect. Your current working directory IS a disposable git worktree containing your previous build. Revise it in place; do not start over.

BOUNDARY, read this before anything else.
- You own exactly three files and may create or modify NOTHING else: scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py, scripts/validate_v21.py, tests/test_v21_scenarios.py. You may also write generated output under build/.
- NEVER run git commit, git push, or any git write command. Leave changes uncommitted; the harness exports them.
- NEVER call a network endpoint or external API. Everything you need is on disk.
- NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory or knowledge base.
- Do not modify contract/decisions.json, contract/review.json, or any v20 reference file.

WHAT IS ON DISK: your previous generator, validator and test suite; contract/decisions.json (the design contract); contract/review.json (the nine findings, read it in full); contract/verified-defects.md; and the v20 reference sources.

THE NINE FIXES. Each is mandatory.

V21-R1, BLOCKING, double booking. Today a patient with a confirmed booking who says "actually, can we do Thursday instead?" enters the global negotiation loop, reaches a sign node, and books a SECOND appointment. The first is never cancelled because every cancel, reschedule and modify operation is blocked at the gateway. The patient is told Thursday is booked and reasonably believes the original was replaced, so they hold two appointments believing they hold one. Fix BOTH ways: (a) n_confirmation's prompt must again direct any post-booking cancel, reschedule or change request to the office at (855) 750-6688 and must never book a second appointment, restoring the defense v20 had and v21 deleted; and (b) n_negotiate's globalLabel must explicitly state it does NOT apply once a booking has been confirmed. Add an edge from n_confirmation to e_existing labelled for the post-booking change request.

V21-R2, timeout can never fire. A global node fires by matching a patient MESSAGE. A 72-hour silence produces no message, so a global e_timeout could never trigger; today there is no timeout mechanism at all and the no_reply outcome is unreachable. Fix: e_timeout is NOT global. Remove isGlobal from it and wire an explicit labelled edge to e_timeout from EVERY patient-waiting node. Remove the rule in validate_v21.py that bans waiting nodes from having physical exit edges to e_timeout; keep that ban for e_stop, e_not_me and e_existing, which do fire on real messages.

V21-R3, the office node dead-ends. n_office has no outgoing edge and no end node. Add an e_office end node and an edge from n_office to it.

V21-R4, a plain decline has nowhere to go. "No thanks" and "not interested" are the most common replies to a recall text and match no edge and no global; the declared declined outcome is unreachable and the model would be forced to record a decline as consent revocation, which is false. Fix: add an e_declined end node carrying the declined outcome, with labelled edges from n_opener_two, n_opener_one and n_negotiate_offer. A decline is NOT an opt-out; do not route it to e_stop and do not record it as opt_out.

V21-R5, the slot-count split is not real. Both slot_count edges converge on one opener node whose single prompt contains both message shapes, so suppressing the second slot is still the model's job. Fix: split the opener into TWO nodes, n_opener_two and n_opener_one, each with exactly one message template. Route slot_count >= 2 to n_opener_two and slot_count == 1 to n_opener_one. Neither prompt may branch on slot_count.

V21-R6, the negotiation lane lets the model retype booking payloads. Today the negotiation loop uses an availability TOOL and the model transcribes slot times from the tool result into pathway variables that template directly into /conflict-check and /sign, so a mis-copied or stale slot can book cleanly. The conflict check only proves the sent slot is free, never that it is the slot the patient chose. Fix: REMOVE the tool entirely. No node may attach a tool. Restructure the lane into three nodes: n_negotiate is a waiting node that collects ONLY the preference variables (preference_from, preference_to, preference_after, preference_before, time_pref) and must NOT extract any slot value; n_search is a silent Webhook posting the gateway /availability route with those preferences templated into its body, whose responseData maps slot_count, slot_1_start, slot_1_end, slot_1_doctor, slot_2_start, slot_2_end, slot_2_doctor and time_pref_relaxed from the gateway response exactly as the v20 availability node does; n_negotiate_offer is a waiting node that offers what the search returned and carries the selection edges to the conflict checks. Route n_search on slot_count: below one back to n_negotiate, one or more to n_negotiate_offer, and a gateway failure to e_safe_failure. This also removes the __MOTT_AVAILABILITY_TOOL_ID__ placeholder, so nothing needs substituting at deploy time.

V21-R7, the tests assume their own conclusion. The effective_adjacency helper unconditionally adds every isGlobal node as a successor of every waiting node, so the reachability tests pass on any graph whose nodes merely carry the flag, proving nothing about the design. The date-passthrough test likewise asserts on a dict the test itself constructs. Fix: reachability assertions must read the graph's DECLARED structure. For globals, assert the specific properties that are actually checkable offline: the node carries isGlobal, its globalLabel is non-empty, its trigger text excludes the cases another global owns, and it has the outgoing edges the design requires. Do not assert that a global is reachable from a node when nothing in the artifact proves that. The date test must assert against the generated n_search webhook body, not a dict built inside the test.

V21-R8, the opener instruction contradicts itself. It says to send a template "verbatim" while also requiring display-only rendering of the very placeholders inside it. Fix: state the rule once and unambiguously. The message wording is fixed; the slot placeholders are replaced with the rendered America/New_York time; the stored slot values used by /conflict-check and /sign are never altered.

V21-R9, mixed replies can be captured by the negotiation global. A reply like "1, but afternoon instead" satisfies the negotiation trigger while also selecting a slot. Fix: n_negotiate's globalLabel must explicitly exclude replies that also select an offered slot, stating those belong to clarification.

INVARIANTS THAT DO NOT CHANGE. Every webhook sets Authorization to exactly {{ SECRET.MottGatewayToken }} and retryAttempts to 0. Booking is /sign only with verb appt.book and reason new-booking and no allow_conflict. The legacy /book, /reschedule and /cancel routes never appear. n_identity is the only start node and still guards an empty or unresolved recall_patient_id before any gateway call. n_confirmation is reachable only on book_success true. The mirrored slot-1 and slot-2 conflict-and-sign spine stays. Every edge carries a non-empty label. No prompt instructs the model to normalize or compute calendar dates. The graph carries analysis_options with the fields from contract/decisions.json, and its outcome enum must include declined. Ceilings: at most 26 nodes and at most 54 edges.

The full node set after your revision is: n_identity, n_availability, n_opener_two, n_opener_one, n_mixed_clarify, n_negotiate, n_search, n_negotiate_offer, n_office, n_conflict_1, n_conflict_2, n_sign_1, n_sign_2, n_confirmation, e_safe_identity, e_safe_failure, e_booking_failed, e_booked, e_office, e_declined, e_stop, e_not_me, e_existing, e_timeout.

ALSO UPDATE THE TESTS to cover the new behavior: a post-confirmation change request never reaches a sign node; every waiting node has an explicit timeout edge; a decline reaches e_declined and not e_stop; the one-slot and two-slot openers are separate nodes with non-branching prompts; no node attaches a tool; and n_search maps all eight slot fields from the gateway response.

HOW TO VERIFY YOUR OWN WORK, from the worktree root:
  mkdir -p build
  python3 scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py --out build/v21_a.json
  python3 scripts/build_v21_recall_lanes.py --out build/v21_b.json
  diff build/v21_a.json build/v21_b.json
  python3 scripts/validate_v21.py
  python3 -m pytest tests/test_v21_scenarios.py -q

All five must succeed. An independent orchestrator-owned gate also runs against your graph and enforces every fix above by finding id, so satisfying only your own validator is not enough.

HARD RULES. Do not invent gateway endpoints, request fields or response paths. Do not weaken a booking safety invariant to simplify the graph. Do not write a test that asserts a property its own helper injects. Do not commit. Do not touch any file outside your three owned paths and build/.
tasks.verified: the revised generator is deterministic and its graph passes the revision-2 orchestrator gate, which enforces every one of the nine review findings by id including the double-booking defense, the explicit timeout wiring, the decline lane and the removal of model-transcribed slot values
